products.superPrompt:
You are an experienced astrology teacher and instructional designer. Your goal: write the complete, print-ready text of a 12-week beginner workbook that teaches someone to read their own Western birth chart step by step, as a reflective and symbolic practice, never as prediction.

BUYER AND JOB
The buyer is a Gen Z or millennial beginner who wants to read their own chart instead of horoscopes (they search phrases like "learn astrology" and "how to read a natal chart"). The workbook gives them a weekly path, a place to record their own chart, and prompts to think about what fits and what doesn't.

DELIVERABLE (number every page)
- P1 Title page: "[PRODUCT TITLE]", subtitle "A 12-week workbook for reading your own birth chart", "[YOUR SHOP NAME]".
- P2 How to use this workbook: one lesson a week (30-45 minutes); you need birth date, time and place; get your chart from any free online chart calculator (do not name sites or apps); if the birth time is unknown, use a noon chart and skip the Ascendant and houses.
- P3 My Chart at a Glance: rows Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, North Node, Ascendant, Midheaven; columns Sign | Degree | House | Retrograde (Y/N).
- P4 My Chart Wheel: how to copy positions onto the blank wheel art (Ascendant at the left, houses 1-12 running counterclockwise).
- Weeks 1-12, three pages each: (a) Lesson, 350-450 words, with one worked example using an invented sample chart; (b) Worksheet with fill-in lines tied to the reader's own chart; (c) Reflection: three prompts, a "What resonates / What doesn't" two-column box, and "Questions I still have".
  Topics: 1 What a birth chart is (Sun, Moon and planet positions as seen from the birthplace at the birth moment; the tropical zodiac most Western astrologers use vs the sidereal zodiac used in Vedic astrology; signs are not the same as constellations). 2 The 12 signs through elements and modalities. 3 Sun and Moon. 4 Mercury, Venus, Mars. 5 Jupiter and Saturn. 6 Uranus, Neptune, Pluto (Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006; astrologers still use it). 7 The Ascendant and the four angles. 8 The 12 houses, and why house systems (Placidus, Whole Sign, Equal) give different results. 9 Planets in houses. 10 Aspects: conjunction 0, sextile 60, square 90, trine 120, opposition 180 degrees; orbs are a convention that varies. 11 Rulerships, retrograde as apparent motion seen from Earth, the lunar nodes. 12 Putting it together: a one-page "chart portrait" in the reader's own words.
  Label P2-P4 and Weeks 1-4 "[SAMPLE]" (they become the free sample).
- Reference tables: Signs (sign, glyph, approximate tropical dates, element, modality, traditional ruler, modern ruler); Planets (planet, glyph, 3-4 neutral themes); Houses (house, commonly associated life areas).
- Glossary: 40 terms, alphabetical, one or two sentences each.
- Keep Learning: five practice ideas using the workbook and invented sample charts.

DESIGN (one layout line per page)
US Letter 8.5x11 in, plus an A4 version; 0.6 in margins; headings Cormorant Garamond, body Lato 11 pt; palette "Night Study": Ink Navy #1F2A44, Parchment #F6F1E7, Brass Gold #C9A227, Dusty Lilac #B8A9C9, Slate #5B6475. Write planet and sign names in full beside every glyph.

CONTENT RULES
Original wording only. Warm, curious, plain tone, about an 8th-grade reading level. Use framing like "astrologers traditionally associate..." or "many practitioners read...", never statements of fact about the reader. Accuracy checks: fire = Aries, Leo, Sagittarius; earth = Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn; air = Gemini, Libra, Aquarius; water = Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces; cardinal = Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn; fixed = Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius; mutable = Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces; traditional/modern rulers of Scorpio Mars/Pluto, Aquarius Saturn/Uranus, Pisces Jupiter/Neptune; sign dates are approximate and shift by a day in some years; the Sun and Moon never go retrograde.

WHY THIS IS BETTER
Unlike sun-sign decor and horoscope journals, it teaches the method: each week builds on the last, everything is applied to the reader's own chart, and the "What doesn't resonate" box welcomes skeptics.

CONSTRAINTS
No predictions, forecasts, compatibility verdicts, or claims about health, money, love or success. No names of astrologers, books, websites, apps, celebrities or real people's charts. No copied text.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Page by page: "=== PAGE [n]: [title] ===", then "Layout:" (one line), then the exact text, with fill-in lines as "______" and tables as pipe tables. If you run out of space, stop at a page break and wait for "continue". End with:
SELF-CHECK (answer yes/no; fix any "no" before replying): every page is present; 12 weeks x 3 pages; elements, modalities and rulers match the checks above; no predictions or outcome promises; no brand, site, app or person names; all wording original.

[PASTE TABLE: phase | date | time ET]
2027 eclipses (from NASA's eclipse website):
[PASTE TABLE: date | type | where visible]

1 Cover: "2027 Moon Phase & Intentions Planner", "[YOUR SHOP NAME]".
2 How to use: one new-moon page and one full-moon page per lunation; times are Eastern; in other time zones a phase can fall on the neighboring date.

- One Full Moon page per full moon in that month: date and time, "What I noticed this cycle", "What's working", "What I'm ready to set down", "Gratitude".

Dates come from an authoritative source with the time zone stated; pages are for reflection, not horoscopes; the design is clean and quiet instead of crowded.

CONSTRAINTS
No predictions; no claims about the Moon's effect on health, sleep, mood, fertility, money, plants or relationships; no "manifest" promises. No brand, app or planner names; no copied layouts.

products.listingPrompt:
You are an Amazon KDP listing copywriter. Write the KDP details for my paperback "Reading Notes: A 365-Entry Bible Reading Journal - [MINIMAL or SOFT] Edition": undated, 384 pages, 6x9 in, one entry per page with fields for date, passage reference, what stood out, questions, and notes or prayer; front pages explain how the Bible is organized and how to read a reference; a books-read checklist with space for the additional books in Catholic and Orthodox Bibles; no scripture text.

Produce:
1. TITLE and SUBTITLE (together under 200 characters), with the subtitle starting with the buyer's search phrase (for example "Bible Reading Journal for ..."). Give 3 options and mark your pick.
2. DESCRIPTION under 2,000 characters using simple HTML (<b>, <ul>, <li>): opener, what's inside, size and page count, who it's for, a neutral line that it works with any translation or reading plan.
3. 7 KEYWORD phrases for the KDP keyword boxes (each under 50 characters, not repeating title words, no brand names).
4. 3 suggested Amazon category paths that fit a Bible reading journal; I will pick the closest available ones.
5. A short Etsy listing for the printable PDF version: title under 140 characters front-loading "Bible Reading Journal", 13 tags of 20 characters or fewer (show each count), and a description with what's included, files (US Letter and A4 PDFs), how delivery works (instant download, nothing ships), one line saying AI tools helped draft it and I checked it, and a 3-question FAQ.

Rules: no ministry, church, app, publisher, translation or reading-plan brand names; no claims about spiritual, emotional or mental-health outcomes; no "bestseller" claims; neutral across Christian traditions; original wording; plain US English.

pricing.rationale: A 384-page paperback costs about $5.60+ to print, so list at $14.99 for a roughly $2.20-$3.40 royalty; sell the printable on Etsy at about $6 and the plan + journal bundle at about $9.
